title: Schema-drift observability + graceful fallback acceptance criteria for streamed function calls
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Problem: Customers are seeing silent degradations when streamed structured outputs deviate from expected schemas during function/tool handoffs. This PRD clarifies acceptance criteria for detecting schema drift in real-time, surfacing developer-friendly errors, driving automatic graceful fallbacks, and providing deterministic telemetry for post-incident diagnosis. Scope: runtime + console observability + SDK surface (streamed events and error envelopes). Out of scope: model training/data collection fixes and long-term schema evolution governance (will be handled in a follow-up project).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Drift detection: The runtime emits a schema-drift event whenever a streamed fragment violates the declared schema more than N=2 times within a single session or when a single violation is classified as fatal (invalid type for top-level required field). Events must include: path, expected type/schema version, actual token sequence snippet (<=512 chars), and a deterministic violation code.

2) Developer error envelope: When a drift is detected the streamed connection must include a final machine-readable error envelope with fields: error_code, human_message, recovery_suggestion (one of: retry_prompt, switch_variant, fallback_payload), example failing_fragment, and trace_id. The envelope must be consumable by SDKs without blocking normal streaming of already-valid frames.

3) Graceful fallback behavior: For non-fatal drift (missing optional keys or minor type coercions), runtime must attempt to auto-correct using predefined coercion rules (string->number, number->string) and continue streaming. If auto-correction is applied, an info-level envelope must be emitted and count toward the session's drift metrics.

4) Canary policy for model variants: If drift rate exceeds 1% of sessions over a 10-minute window for a given model variant, system must route new sessions to the pinned-compatible fallback variant and mark the original variant as read-only for rollouts. This routing change must be reversible via console with a single click and an audit log entry.

5) Observability and SLIs: Console dashboards must display per-model and per-route metrics: schema_violation_rate (per 1k sessions), median-time-to-detect (ms), percent_auto_corrected, and percent_session_fallback. Alerts: page when schema_violation_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m for customers with >1k sessions/min.

6) Backwards compatibility gate: When deploying schema changes, the runtime must support a 'compatibility window' header that allows serving both old and new schemas for a configurable grace period (default 72h). During the window the system will emit negotiation telemetry with counts of old vs new consumers.

7) SDK ergonomics: SDKs must surface a typed SchemaDrift exception with attributes: path, expected_schema_hash, observed_samples (list of up to 3 string snippets), suggested_action. SDK must provide a helper to auto-generate a minimal repro prompt and attach the relevant trace_id to a support ticket template.

8) Test harness: Every release must include an automated test suite that simulates: single-frame fatal violations, streaming fragment reordering, partial object emissions, and intermittent token corruption. Each test must assert deterministic error envelopes and the presence of the trace_id in telemetry.

9) Performance constraints: Drift detection and envelope emission must add no more than 2ms p99 overhead to the critical token path under normal throughput (validated in perf runs), and must not increase median latency by >5% for small payloads (<512 tokens).

10) Security and PII: Any sample snippets emitted in telemetry must be redacted of high-risk PII (emails, SSNs, credit card numbers) before leaving the customer's VPC or being stored in logs. The runtime must honor customer-configured redaction policies and document the default redaction rules.
test_cases: TC-01: Simulate top-level required field type mismatch in a single-frame stream -> expect fatal schema-drift event, final error envelope with error_code: DRIFT_FATAL, and session terminated flag in telemetry.
TC-02: Streamed object that omits an optional key twice -> expect auto-correction path to insert default value, info envelope emitted, session completes normally, percent_auto_corrected increments.

TC-03: Reordered fragments that temporarily break JSON assembly -> expect runtime to buffer up to 3 fragments, attempt reassembly, and if unsuccessful emit DRIFT_TRANSIENT with suggested_action: retry_prompt.
TC-04: Canary trigger: create synthetic traffic to push schema_violation_rate above 1% for a model variant -> expect new sessions routed to fallback, console flag set, and an audit log entry created.
TC-05: SDK surface test: call streaming API and capture SchemaDrift exception -> assert exception fields populated and repro helper produces a valid minimal repro with trace_id.

TC-06: PII redaction: include email and credit card patterns in failing fragment -> assert stored telemetry has redacted values and console raw-snippet preview is masked unless customer has explicit data retention override.
TC-07: Performance smoke: run drift detection under 95th percentile throughput for a scaled cluster and measure overhead <=2ms p99.
TC-08: Backcompat header: deploy schema change with compatibility window and assert negotiation telemetry shows >95% compatibility before window end for a controlled consumer group.

TC-09: Streaming token corruption: inject single-token corruption mid-object and expect DRIFT_CORRUPTION with recovery_suggestion: switch_variant; verify fallback path executes without leaking partial PII.
TC-10: Observability alert: synthetic workload triggers sustained 0.6% violation rate for 6 minutes -> expect oncall page and Slack alert, with runbook link attached.
